title: This Free Workout Tracker Knows You Skipped Leg Day
description:
A free workout tracker app you run yourself: openGym is an open-source (AGPL-3.0), self-hosted gym and body-weight tracker. No subscription, no ads, no telemetry, and your data stays in one folder you own. It picked up 6,749 GitHub stars this week.

What it does
• Over 5,600 exercises with animated demos, browsable by muscle on a body map; filter by the equipment you own.
• Guided workouts: last time's weights pre-filled, a rest timer, and new records spotted as they happen.
• Plate math for barbell, EZ bar, trap bar and Smith machine, worked out from the plates you own.
• A muscle map in three modes: where your volume went, what's still recovering, and what's gone untrained.
• Progression rules (linear, Greyskull LP, double and triple progression); missed reps never add load, stalls trigger a deload.
• Imports from Strong, Hevy and FitNotes; exports everything as one JSON file.
• Passkey sign-in, works offline, syncs your phone and laptop (two devices editing at once merge field by field).
• Optional extras: an AI coach that runs with your own provider key and changes nothing until you approve it, and a read-only MCP server so an assistant like Claude can answer questions about your training.

How to run it
One `docker compose up -d` on your own machine. Everything lives in ./data: back up that folder and you've backed up everything. Passkeys on a phone need HTTPS on a domain. On iPhone it's a web app (PWA); the Android app runs entirely on the phone, with no server.
